name: Elah
overview: Elah was a male figure in the Old Testament, known primarily as the son of Baasha and as a King of Israel. His role as a monarch is recorded in 1 Kings 16:6, establishing his significance within the history of Israel's monarchy. No additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are provided in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Elah is a proper name meaning "species of a mighty tree," as noted in 1 Kings 16:6. This name does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a strong and enduring image consistent with his royal status.
familyAndRelationships: Elah is explicitly identified as the son of Baasha in 1 Kings 16:8. Additionally, he is associated with Zimri as a victim, an inferred relationship noted in 1 Kings 16:9. Beyond these, Scripture does not record further family relationships for Elah.
scriptureSignificance: Elah's significance in Scripture centers on his role as a king of Israel and the continuation of Baasha's dynasty. His reign is part of the unfolding narrative of Israel's monarchy, illustrating the often turbulent succession and challenges to the throne. His death at the hands of Zimri marks a pivotal moment in the kingdom's history, highlighting the instability during this period.
